solver_notes: The issue metadata names torvalds/linux, but Python/pylifecycle.c is CPython code; the tested base is python/cpython v3.12.0 commit 0fb18b02c8ad56299d6a2910be0bab8ad601ef24. The actual delete and SaveThread implementations are Python/pystate.c and Python/ceval_gil.c, so the patch touches those files plus Include/cpython/pystate.h rather than pretending the Linux repository contains pylifecycle.c. PyEval_SaveThread now takes runtime head_mutex across SwapNoGIL and atomic pin acquisition, holds the pin through drop_gil, then uses atomic decrement with release ordering. PyInterpreterState_Delete detaches the interpreter and thread lists under head_mutex, drains gil_release_refs with acquire loads before each free, then finalizes the interpreter. The deterministic model reproduces the legacy free-while-pinned ordering and verifies the fixed drain and no-pin baseline. The real patched CPython built successfully on RakMiner-B aarch64 and passed its threading, subinterpreter, and embedding suites. Scope: this pins an already-entered SaveThread critical section; it does not make arbitrary stale tstate pointers valid after API lifetime violations, nor does it claim a deterministic upstream race reproduction. An optional ASan+UBSan build could not initialize ASan on this Pi runtime (sanitizer allocator CHECK before main); UBSan-only execution passed and the ASan initialization failure is not reported as a test pass.

ordinary no-pin delete and mutex baseline pass
